Circular bioeconomy  ·  Malaysia

From durian husk to durable soil value.

We turn Malaysia's tropical fruit and palm waste into biochar, bio-oil, carbon credits and functional food ingredients, one circular platform, five revenue layers.

Request the investor deckSee how it works
The problem

A billion-dollar resource is being burned and buried.

Malaysia generates millions of tonnes of fruit and palm residues every year. Most are burned in the open or landfilled, releasing CO₂ and methane while farm soils lose organic matter.

500,000 tDurian husk & shell waste per year, from just two harvests
80M+ tPalm biomass waste per year
~200,000 tPineapple waste per year
~800,000 tBanana biomass potentially available per year

Figures are published industry estimates and vary by source and year.

Our solution

One platform. Three streams from waste.

Controlled pyrolysis at 400 to 700°C, without oxygen, converts biomass into stable carbon products instead of smoke.

1

Biochar

A stable, carbon-rich soil amendment sold as organic fertilizer. Improves water retention and nutrient efficiency. Our near-term revenue engine.

2

Bio-oil

A recoverable liquid energy stream from the same reactor, sold to industrial fuel buyers as a secondary product.

3

Carbon credits

Biochar locks carbon in soil for centuries, roughly 2.5 t CO₂e per tonne applied. Credits trade at USD 50 to 100 per tonne, a higher-margin stream than burning syngas.

By-product syngas is recirculated to power the reactor itself, so the plant runs energy self-sufficient after start-up.

1. CollectSecure feedstock from durian farms, palm mills and fruit processors.
2. PrepareDry, shred and condition biomass for stable throughput.
3. ConvertControlled pyrolysis locks carbon into a stable solid.
4. RecoverSeparate biochar, bio-oil and syngas from the reactor.
5. FormulateTurn outputs into tested farm-ready and food-grade products.
Feedstock strategy

Durian is the flagship. Diversity keeps the plant running.

Durian fruits only twice a year. A durian-only plant would sit idle between harvests, so we blend in palm, pineapple and banana residues that are available almost year-round.

Durian season
Palm / pineapple / banana
Durian season
Palm / pineapple / banana

Illustrative supply pattern. Durian husk and seed remain our highest-value feedstock.

The differentiator

Durian seeds are a food-ingredient platform, not just waste.

Published food-science research shows durian seed is rich in starch and dietary fibre, with protein, unsaturated fats and antioxidant compounds.

  • Roughly 46% carbohydrate/starch: suited to flour and starch extraction
  • Phenolic, flavonoid and antioxidant compounds: nutraceutical potential
  • Demonstrated in high-fibre biscuits, cakes, noodles and as a natural thickener
  • A premium, food-grade revenue line on top of soil products

Product claims and food-grade approvals will follow local regulatory testing.

Market opportunity

A fast-growing market, with a feedstock advantage.

The global biochar market is projected to grow from about USD 1.2B in 2023 to USD 4.8B by 2030, roughly 22% a year, driven by carbon-removal credits and sustainable-agriculture inputs.

  • Biochar qualifies as a carbon dioxide removal (CDR) method
  • Carbon credits currently trade at about USD 50 to 100 per tonne CO₂
  • Domestic organic-fertilizer demand growing about 15% a year

Global biochar market size, USD. Third-party market estimate.

Projected growth

From pilot to a USD 6M+ regional platform in five years.

Year one proves the pilot. Years two and three add carbon credits and seed ingredients. Years four and five replicate the model across Malaysia and ASEAN.

  • Year 5 mix: soil products 35%, carbon credits 25%, functional ingredients 20%, bio-oil 15%, licensing 5%
  • Break-even targeted within 18 to 24 months of commissioning the pilot
  • Growth beyond Year 5 through additional processing hubs

Illustrative projection (USD) based on phased scale-up. Assumes carbon-credit methodology registration by Year 2 and seed-ingredient sales from Year 2 to 3. To be refined with pilot data. Not a guarantee of results.

Roadmap

From pilot to regional platform.

YEAR 1  PILOT & PROVE

  • Commission the demonstration plant
  • Secure durian and palm feedstock agreements
  • First biochar and fertilizer sales to partner farms
  • Initial durian seed-flour trials

YEAR 2  OPTIMIZE

  • Onboard pineapple and banana feedstock
  • Register carbon-credit methodology
  • Launch the seed-ingredient product line
  • Standardize biochar quality

YEARS 3 TO 5+  EXPAND

  • Second and third hubs across Malaysia and ASEAN
  • R&D licensing for durian-fibre materials
  • Full five-stream revenue mix at scale

Impact across soil, climate and livelihoods

  • Environmental: diverts biomass from open burning and landfill; stores carbon in soil; improves water retention
  • Economic: a bio-based value chain with direct jobs in the plant and field, and indirect jobs in collection and transport
  • Innovation: a tropical, durian-focused biochar and seed-ingredient platform with room for IP and licensing
